transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-06 16:00 PST
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jenna (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM); Ethan (NovusRetail VP Eng), Sara (Platform Eng), Laila (Security Lead), Arjun (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, brief):
- Kickoff / immersion for NovusRetail pilot deployment.
- Main concerns: latency SLOs for store search, VPC connectivity, SOC2-like audit evidence, and quantization tradeoffs.
- Agreed next steps: staging access, bench, and security doc handoff.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jenna (AE): Hey everyone thanks for carving time, quick intros?
[00:07] Ethan (VP Eng): Ethan here, VP Eng at NovusRetail, leading infra and search.
[00:12] Sara (Platform Eng): Sara, I own platform and infra bits, will do the staging networking.
[00:17] Laila (Security): Laila, security lead, focusing on data residency and audit logs.
[00:22] Arjun (PM): Arjun product, owner for search relevance.
[00:25] Jenna: Great, from Redwood Marco our SE and Priya our CSM, quick goal: get pilot running in staging, validate latency+cost for product search.
[00:35] Marco (SE): Hi all, I'll be driving the bench and runtime questions, happy to dig into batching/kv cache.
[00:40] Priya (CSM): I'll coordinate timelines and access.

[02:00] Jenna: To frame it, NovusRetail's target is 95th pct latency under 300ms for p99? sorry p95, and cost per 1k queries under $X — Arjun correct me.
[02:12] Arjun: Right, p95 under 300ms for 256-token avg responses, budget is tight for pilot.
[02:20] Ethan: We're evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated — prefer Hosted for fast start but might need Dedicated for SLOs later.

[04:05] Marco: Quick note: hosting can usually get you close, but Dedicated gives predictable throughput. Also quantization profile will change both latency and quality.
[04:15] Sara: When you say quantization profile can you give a concrete example, like int8 vs fp16 impact?
[04:22] Marco: Sure, int8 (our Q8 path) drops memory and cost, adds some delta in generation quality on long form, for retrieval-type short answers it's usually fine. We'll show side-by-side eval.

[06:30] Laila: On security we need SOC2 attestation, audit logs for token-level queries, and KMS integration. Are those baked into Redwood Private?
[06:40] Priya: Yes we have doc pack — will share SOC2 & ISO snippets, plus KMS/HSM integration notes. For Private you can manage keys, for Dedicated we can also key wrap.
[06:55] Laila: Also need data retention policy — can we set token retention to zero for certain routes?
[07:05] Marco: We can set per-route retention and TTLs; love to get a list of sensitive routes so we can match policies.

[09:10] Ethan: Network wise, we want to use VPC peering to staging, no public egress if possible.
[09:18] Sara: I'll open a peering ticket, need Redwood IP ranges.
[09:22] Jenna: We'll send the allowlist and peering template — note sometimes the egress path requires a NAT for certain calls, we'll document.

[11:50] Arjun: What's the typical bench you run for ecom search? do you simulate cart + query concurrency?
[11:58] Marco: We do a shard of workloads: 50/50 short queries vs context windows ~512 tokens, do concurrency sweeps (1-200 qps) and measure tail latencies and token cost. For your target p95 we'll run a 8k token-sweep and a 30-minute steady-state test.

[14:20] Sara: For the bench, can Marco run it against our staging cluster or do you need Redwood-provided staging?
[14:28] Marco: We prefer running against your staging so network and infra match — Redwood can stand up a temporary model endpoint if you want to compare Hosted vs Dedicated flavors.

[16:05] Ethan: A practical question: what are the fallbacks if model capacity is constrained during high traffic?
[16:12] Priya: We have routing policies — can fallback to smaller model variant, cross-region fallback, or queue and spill to dedicated pool. We'll show failover graphs.

[18:40] Laila: We need to understand logs for audit — tokens, request metadata, user IDs — how granular?
[18:48] Marco: We log request IDs, token counts, timestamps, model variant, and optionally masked prompt hashes for privacy. Full PII should not be in logs.

[20:10] Sara: Any gotchas on SAML SSO for our team? we use Okta.
[20:16] Priya: We support SAML/Okta, will send the SSO runbook. For RBAC we map to roles and route-level permissions.

[22:00] Arjun: On prompt engineering — do you help curate prompt sets for evals?
[22:06] Marco: Yes SEs can run eval harnesses, we can import your labelled prompts and run regression checks across model/quantization changes.

[24:30] Ethan: Cost: how predictable is the cost on Hosted when concurrency spikes — are there mechanisms to cap spend?
[24:40] Jenna: You can set quotas/alerts, and route-level caps. For strict spend controls we recommend Dedicated with burst policies.

[27:15] Sara: We plan to test with our existing cache layer in front, any recommended cache TTLs?
[27:22] Marco: For search you can prefix-cache frequent queries, TTLs vary but 5-30s often gives big wins while preserving freshness. Also KV cache at the runtime layer preserves attention state for multi-turn.

[30:05] Laila: Compliance question — can we get an artifact catalog of where data is stored (logs, model caches)?
[30:12] Priya: Yes, we'll provide a data flow diagram and storage matrix. We'll include KV cache retention behavior and options for in-memory only paths.

[32:30] Arjun: Timelines: we'd like a pilot in staging within 2 weeks and a decision on Dedicated vs Hosted by end of month. Feasible?
[32:40] Jenna: Feasible if we get staging access and firewall rules in the next 3 business days. Marco can do perf bench in week 2.

[34:50] Sara: One small note — our infra requires TLS mutual auth for peered endpoints. Can Redwood support mTLS on the endpoint?
[34:58] Marco: We can support mTLS in Dedicated and Private; for hosted endpoints we'll need a gateway in front — we'll include options in the runbook.

[37:00] Ethan: Any reference customers in retail? any benchmarks you can share?
[37:07] Jenna: We'll share anonymized retail case studies and a short benchmark deck. Note that numbers vary by model and token sizes.

[39:20] Priya: Ok recap: Jenna will send pricing + decision guide; Marco will schedule perf bench with Sara; Priya will share SOC2 and SSO runbook; Sara to send allowlist and peering ticket.

[40:00] Laila: Quick clarification, if we go Dedicated, what's the SLA and commit terms?
[40:07] Jenna: Dedicated has an SLA we can include in the contract; options for monthly committed throughput or annual. We'll outline options in the pricing doc.

[42:10] Arjun: Could you also include a short runbook for rollback strategies and A/B model rollouts?
[42:18] Marco: Yes, can include canary policies, A/B split examples, and automatic fallback configs.

[44:00] Jenna: Thanks everyone, action items as we discussed. We'll follow up with links and calendar invites for the bench.
[44:10] Ethan: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.

Shared artifacts referenced:
- Staging runbook (to be sent)
- SSO + SOC2 bundle (link provided by Priya)
- Benchmark template (SE bench sheet)
- Pricing + Dedicated decision guide (to be sent)

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings on product names ("Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Redwood Dedicated"), speaker overlap around 16:00-17:00 when multiple people chimed in.
